adam.name: Adam
adam.role: First ancestor in the family list
adam.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
adam.importance: His name opens the book. The list gives only his name, then Seth and Enosh.
adam.connections: Partner of Eve. Father of Cain, Abel, and Seth.

enoch.name: Enoch
enoch.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
enoch.importance: The list names him between Jared and Methuselah. It tells no story about him.
enoch.connections: Descendant of Seth. Father of Methuselah.

noah.name: Noah
noah.role: Ancestor of the three listed family branches
noah.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
noah.importance: The list names him after Lamech. It then names Shem, Ham, and Japheth and follows their families.
noah.connections: Father of Shem, Ham, and Japheth.

shem.name: Shem
shem.role: Noah’s son and ancestor of Abraham
shem.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
shem.importance: The list names his sons, starting with Elam and Asshur. It then runs from Shem through Arpachshad and Eber to Abram.
shem.connections: Brother of Ham and Japheth. Ancestor of Abraham.

ham.name: Ham
ham.role: Noah’s son and ancestor of neighboring peoples
ham.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
ham.importance: His sons are Cush, Mizraim, Put, and Canaan. The list names Nimrod, the Jebusite, and the Amorite in this branch.
ham.connections: Father of Canaan. Brother of Shem and Japheth.

japheth.name: Japheth
japheth.role: Noah’s son in the first listed branch
japheth.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
japheth.importance: His seven sons come first in the list, starting with Gomer. The list then names the sons of Gomer and Javan. It tells no story about him.

nimrod.name: Nimrod
nimrod.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
nimrod.importance: Cush is his father. The list says he began to be a mighty one on the earth. It says no more about him.

abraham.name: Abraham
abraham.role: Ancestor remembered in family lists and praise
abraham.life: Historical birth and death years are not securely known.
abraham.importance: The list calls him Abram, also called Abraham. It names his sons Isaac and Ishmael, then the sons of Keturah. David’s song recalls the covenant God made with him. David’s last prayer calls the LORD the God of Abraham, Isaac, and Israel.
abraham.connections: Husband of Sarah. Father of Ishmael and Isaac. Uncle of Lot.

ishmael.name: Ishmael
ishmael.role: Abraham’s son with a named descendant list
ishmael.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
ishmael.importance: He is a son of Abraham. The list names his twelve sons, from Nebaioth to Kedemah. It then turns to Keturah’s sons and to Isaac.
ishmael.connections: Half-brother of Isaac. Father of twelve named sons.

isaac.name: Isaac
isaac.role: Abraham’s son, named in the list and in praise
isaac.life: Historical birth and death years are not securely known.
isaac.importance: He is Abraham’s son, and his sons are Esau and Israel. David’s song recalls God’s oath to Isaac. David’s last prayer names him with Abraham and Israel.
isaac.connections: Husband of Rebekah. Father of Esau and Jacob.

esau.name: Esau
esau.life: Historical birth and death years are not securely known.
esau.importance: He is Isaac’s son. The list names his five sons and their sons. It then lists the kings and chiefs of Edom.
esau.connections: Twin brother of Jacob. Ancestor of Edom.

jacob.name: Jacob
jacob.role: Israel’s ancestor recalled in families and praise
jacob.life: Historical birth and death years are not securely known.
jacob.importance: The family list calls him Israel and names his twelve sons. David’s song calls the people children of Jacob. It says God confirmed the covenant to Jacob. David’s last prayer names Israel with Abraham and Isaac.
jacob.connections: Son of Isaac and Rebekah. Father of twelve sons and Dinah.

keturah.name: Keturah
keturah.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
keturah.importance: She bears six sons, from Zimran to Shuah. The list also names the sons of Jokshan and Midian. It tells no story about her.
keturah.connections: Abraham’s concubine. Mother of six sons named here.

judah.name: Judah
judah.role: Ancestor of the line leading to David
judah.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
judah.importance: He has five sons. Shua’s daughter bears three, and Tamar bears Perez and Zerah. The LORD kills his firstborn, Er, who was wicked. Chapter 5 says Judah prevailed above his brothers, and the prince came from him.
judah.connections: Son of Jacob and Leah. Father of Perez and Zerah through Tamar.

tamar.name: Tamar
tamar.role: Mother of Perez and Zerah in Judah’s line
tamar.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
tamar.importance: She is Judah’s daughter-in-law. She bears him Perez and Zerah. The line to David runs through Perez and Hezron.
tamar.connections: Widow of Er and Onan. Mother of Perez and Zerah.

boaz.name: Boaz
boaz.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
boaz.importance: The list names him as Salma’s son and Obed’s father. It tells no story about him.
boaz.connections: From Elimelech’s family. Husband of Ruth and father of Obed.

obed.name: Obed
obed.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
obed.importance: He is the son of Boaz and the father of Jesse. The list tells no story about him.
obed.connections: Grandfather of David through Jesse. Naomi cares for him.

jesse.name: Jesse
jesse.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
jesse.importance: He has seven sons. Eliab is the firstborn, and David is the seventh. Later chapters call David the son of Jesse.
jesse.connections: Son of Obed. Father of seven sons and of Zeruiah and Abigail.

david.name: David
david.role: King who brings the ark and prepares the temple
david.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
david.importance: All Israel anoints David king at Hebron, and he takes Jerusalem. He brings the ark there and sets Levites to sing before it. God tells him that his son will build the temple. David counts Israel, buys Ornan’s threshing floor, and gathers gold, stone, and cedar. He gives Solomon the plans and dies at a good old age.
david.connections: Son of Jesse. Father of Amnon, Absalom, Tamar, Solomon, and other children.

zeruiah.name: Zeruiah
zeruiah.role: Woman whose sons lead David’s forces
zeruiah.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
zeruiah.importance: The list names her as a sister of Jesse’s sons. Her sons are Abishai, Joab, and Asahel. Later chapters call Joab and Abishai sons of Zeruiah. The book tells no story about her.
zeruiah.connections: Sister of David. Mother of Abishai, Joab, and Asahel.

abigail-sister.name: Abigail, David’s sister
abigail-sister.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
abigail-sister.importance: She is a sister of David and Zeruiah. She bears Amasa to Jether the Ishmaelite. David’s wife Abigail the Carmelitess is another woman.
abigail-sister.connections: Daughter of Jesse. Sister of David and Zeruiah. Mother of Amasa.

joab.name: Joab
joab.role: Army chief who objects to David’s count
joab.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
joab.importance: He goes up first against the Jebusites, and David makes him chief. He defeats the Syrians and later strikes Rabbah. He objects when David orders the count. He counts Israel but leaves out Levi and Benjamin.
joab.connections: Son of Zeruiah. Brother of Abishai and Asahel.

abishai.name: Abishai
abishai.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
abishai.importance: He lifts his spear against three hundred and kills them. He is made captain of the three. He strikes eighteen thousand Edomites in the Valley of Salt. The children of Ammon flee before him when Joab defeats the Syrians.
abishai.connections: Son of Zeruiah and brother of Joab.

asahel.name: Asahel
asahel.role: David’s nephew among the mighty men
asahel.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
asahel.importance: He is one of Zeruiah’s three sons. The list of mighty men names him in 11:26. He leads the army division for the fourth month. His son Zebadiah leads it after him.
asahel.connections: Brother of Joab and Abishai. Son of Zeruiah.

amasa.name: Amasa
amasa.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
amasa.importance: Abigail bears him to Jether the Ishmaelite. The list tells no story about him.
amasa.connections: Son of Abigail and Jether the Ishmaelite. Nephew of David.

caleb-hezron.name: Caleb, son of Hezron
caleb-hezron.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
caleb-hezron.importance: He has children by Azubah and by Jerioth. After Azubah dies he marries Ephrath, who bears Hur. Hur’s grandson is Bezalel. A second list names more sons, two concubines, and his daughter Achsah. Chapter 4 names a Caleb who is Jephunneh’s son.
caleb-hezron.connections: Son of Hezron. Brother of Jerahmeel.

jarha.name: Jarha
jarha.role: Egyptian servant who marries Sheshan’s daughter
jarha.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
jarha.importance: He is an Egyptian servant of Sheshan. Sheshan has no sons, so he gives Jarha his daughter as wife. She bears Attai. The list follows their family from Attai down to Elishama.
jarha.connections: Servant of Sheshan. Marries Sheshan’s daughter and fathers Attai.

amnon.name: Amnon
amnon.role: David’s firstborn in the royal family list
amnon.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
amnon.importance: He is David’s firstborn, born at Hebron. His mother is Ahinoam the Jezreelitess. The list tells no story about him.
amnon.connections: Son of Ahinoam. Half-brother of Tamar and Absalom.

abigail.name: Abigail
abigail.role: David’s wife in Daniel’s birth notice
abigail.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
abigail.importance: The list calls her Abigail the Carmelitess. She bears Daniel, David’s second son, at Hebron. David’s sister Abigail in chapter 2 is another woman.
abigail.connections: Called the Carmelitess. Wife of David and mother of Daniel.

ahinoam-david.name: Ahinoam
ahinoam-david.role: Mother of Amnon in the royal family list
ahinoam-david.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
ahinoam-david.importance: The list calls her Ahinoam the Jezreelitess. She bears Amnon, David’s firstborn, at Hebron. The list tells no story about her.
ahinoam-david.connections: Called the Jezreelitess. Mother of David’s firstborn, Amnon.

absalom.name: Absalom
absalom.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
absalom.importance: He is David’s third son, born at Hebron. His mother is Maacah, the daughter of Talmai king of Geshur. The list tells no story about him.
absalom.connections: Son of Maacah. Tamar’s brother. Father of a daughter also named Tamar.

adonijah.name: Adonijah
adonijah.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
adonijah.importance: He is David’s fourth son, born at Hebron. His mother is Haggith. The list tells no story about him.
adonijah.connections: Son of David and Haggith. Half-brother of Solomon.

bathsheba.name: Bathshua
bathsheba.role: Bathshua, mother of four named royal sons
bathsheba.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
bathsheba.importance: The list calls her Bathshua, the daughter of Ammiel. She bears David four sons in Jerusalem: Shimea, Shobab, Nathan, and Solomon. The book of Samuel words her name and family differently.
bathsheba.connections: Daughter of Ammiel in 3:5. Mother of four sons of David.

solomon.name: Solomon
solomon.role: David’s son chosen to build the temple
solomon.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
solomon.importance: He is born in Jerusalem to David and Bathshua. David tells him to build the LORD’s house and gives him the plans. The assembly anoints him, and he sits on the throne. All Israel obeys him.
solomon.connections: Son of David and Bathsheba. Father of Rehoboam.

tamar-david.name: Tamar
tamar-david.role: David’s daughter listed after his sons
tamar-david.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
tamar-david.importance: The list names her after David’s sons as their sister. It tells no story about her. Judah’s daughter-in-law Tamar in chapter 2 is another woman.
tamar-david.connections: Daughter of David. Sister of Absalom and half-sister of Amnon.

rehoboam.name: Rehoboam
rehoboam.role: King of Judah in David’s royal line
rehoboam.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
rehoboam.importance: The list names him as Solomon’s son and Abijah’s father. It tells no story about him.
rehoboam.connections: Son of Solomon and Naamah. Father of Abijah.

asa.name: Asa
asa.role: King of Judah in David’s royal line
asa.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
asa.importance: The list places him between Abijah and Jehoshaphat. It tells no story about him.
asa.connections: Son of Abijah. Father of Jehoshaphat.

jehoshaphat.name: Jehoshaphat
jehoshaphat.role: King of Judah in David’s royal line
jehoshaphat.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
jehoshaphat.importance: The list places him between Asa and Joram. It tells no story about him.
jehoshaphat.connections: Son of Asa and Azubah. Father of Jehoram.

jehoram-judah.name: Jehoram, king of Judah
jehoram-judah.role: King of Judah in David’s royal line
jehoram-judah.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
jehoram-judah.importance: The list calls him Joram. It places him between Jehoshaphat and Ahaziah. It tells no story about him.
jehoram-judah.connections: Son of Jehoshaphat. Father of Ahaziah.

ahaziah-judah.name: Ahaziah, king of Judah
ahaziah-judah.role: King of Judah in David’s royal line
ahaziah-judah.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
ahaziah-judah.importance: The list places him between Joram and Joash. It tells no story about him.
ahaziah-judah.connections: Son of Jehoram. Athaliah is his mother. Father of Joash.

joash-judah.name: Joash, king of Judah
joash-judah.role: King of Judah in David’s royal line
joash-judah.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
joash-judah.importance: The list places him between Ahaziah and Amaziah. It tells no story about him.
joash-judah.connections: Son of Ahaziah and Zibiah. Father of Amaziah. Also called Jehoash.

amaziah.name: Amaziah
amaziah.role: King of Judah in David’s royal line
amaziah.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
amaziah.importance: The list places him between Joash and Azariah. It tells no story about him.
amaziah.connections: Son of Joash and Jehoaddan. Father of Azariah.

azariah.name: Azariah
azariah.role: King of Judah in David’s royal line
azariah.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
azariah.importance: The list calls him Azariah. It places him between Amaziah and Jotham. Second Chronicles also uses the name Uzziah.
azariah.connections: Son of Amaziah. Father of Jotham.

jotham.name: Jotham
jotham.role: King of Judah in David’s royal line
jotham.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
jotham.importance: The list places him between Azariah and Ahaz. Chapter 5 says the families of Gad were listed in his days.
jotham.connections: Son of Azariah. Father of Ahaz.

ahaz.name: Ahaz
ahaz.role: King of Judah in David’s royal line
ahaz.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
ahaz.importance: The list places him between Jotham and Hezekiah. It tells no story about him.
ahaz.connections: Son of Jotham. Father of Hezekiah.

hezekiah.name: Hezekiah
hezekiah.role: King of Judah in David’s royal line
hezekiah.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
hezekiah.importance: The list places him between Ahaz and Manasseh. In his days, men of Simeon take pasture land near Gedor (chapter 4).
hezekiah.connections: Son of Ahaz and Abi. Father of Manasseh.

manasseh-king.name: Manasseh, king of Judah
manasseh-king.role: King of Judah in David’s royal line
manasseh-king.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
manasseh-king.importance: The list places him between Hezekiah and Amon. It tells no story about him.
manasseh-king.connections: Son of Hezekiah and Hephzibah. Father of Amon.

amon-king.name: Amon, king of Judah
amon-king.role: King of Judah in David’s royal line
amon-king.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
amon-king.importance: The list places him between Manasseh and Josiah. It tells no story about him.
amon-king.connections: Son of Manasseh and Meshullemeth. Father of Josiah.

josiah.name: Josiah
josiah.role: King of Judah in David’s royal line
josiah.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
josiah.importance: He is Amon’s son. The list names his four sons: Johanan, Jehoiakim, Zedekiah, and Shallum. From here the list follows Jehoiakim’s family.
josiah.connections: Son of Amon and Jedidah. Father of Johanan, Jehoiakim, Zedekiah, and Shallum.

jehoiakim.name: Jehoiakim
jehoiakim.role: King of Judah in David’s royal line
jehoiakim.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
jehoiakim.importance: He is Josiah’s second son. The list names Jeconiah and Zedekiah under him. It follows Jeconiah’s sons next.
jehoiakim.connections: Son of Josiah and Zebidah. Earlier name Eliakim. Father of Jehoiachin.

jehoiachin.name: Jehoiachin
jehoiachin.role: King of Judah in David’s royal line
jehoiachin.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
jehoiachin.importance: The list calls him Jeconiah, the captive. It names his sons, starting with Shealtiel. The family line runs on through Pedaiah and Zerubbabel.
jehoiachin.connections: Son of Jehoiakim and Nehushta. Nephew of Zedekiah.

zedekiah.name: Zedekiah
zedekiah.role: King of Judah in David’s royal line
zedekiah.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
zedekiah.importance: He is the third son of Josiah in the list. It tells no story about him. Verse 16 names another Zedekiah after Jeconiah.
zedekiah.connections: Son of Josiah and Hamutal. Uncle of Jehoiachin. Earlier name Mattaniah.

zedekiah-jeconiah.name: Zedekiah, in Jeconiah’s line
zedekiah-jeconiah.role: Name in the descendants of Jehoiakim
zedekiah-jeconiah.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
zedekiah-jeconiah.importance: Verse 16 lists him after Jeconiah, under the sons of Jehoiakim. The list tells no story about him. Verse 15 names a Zedekiah among Josiah’s sons.
zedekiah-jeconiah.connections: Listed after Jeconiah among the sons of Jehoiakim in 3:16.

zerubbabel.name: Zerubbabel
zerubbabel.role: Descendant in the royal line after captivity
zerubbabel.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
zerubbabel.importance: The list names him as a son of Pedaiah. His children include Meshullam, Hananiah, and their sister Shelomith. Ezra calls him Shealtiel’s son.
zerubbabel.connections: Listed as Pedaiah’s son. Brother of Shimei.

shelomith-daughter.name: Shelomith, Zerubbabel’s daughter
shelomith-daughter.role: Zerubbabel’s daughter in the royal list
shelomith-daughter.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
shelomith-daughter.importance: The list names her as the sister of Meshullam and Hananiah. It tells no story about her.
shelomith-daughter.connections: Daughter of Zerubbabel. Sister of Meshullam and Hananiah.

jabez.name: Jabez
jabez.role: Man whose prayer breaks into the family list
jabez.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
jabez.importance: He is more honorable than his brothers. He asks God to bless him and enlarge his border. He asks God to keep him from evil. God grants what he asks.
jabez.connections: His mother names him. She says she bore him with sorrow.

bithiah.name: Bithiah
bithiah.role: Pharaoh’s daughter in a Judah family record
bithiah.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
bithiah.importance: She is a daughter of Pharaoh, and Mered takes her as wife. Verse 18 speaks of her sons. It is not clear which names are hers.
bithiah.connections: Daughter of an unnamed Pharaoh. Wife of Mered.

caleb.name: Caleb
caleb.role: Son of Jephunneh who receives Hebron’s fields
caleb.life: Historical birth and death years are not securely known.
caleb.importance: His sons are Iru, Elah, and Naam. In chapter 6 he receives the fields and villages of Hebron. The sons of Aaron receive the city and its pasture lands. Chapter 2 names a Caleb who is Hezron’s son.
caleb.connections: Son of Jephunneh. Father of Iru, Elah, and Naam.

simeon.name: Simeon
simeon.role: Son of Israel whose tribe lives near Beersheba
simeon.life: Historical birth and death years are not securely known.
simeon.importance: His sons are Nemuel, Jamin, Jarib, Zerah, and Shaul. His families live at Beersheba, Ziklag, and other towns until David’s reign. They do not grow like the children of Judah. Later some take pasture near Gedor, and five hundred go to Mount Seir.
simeon.connections: Son of Israel. Father of Nemuel, Jamin, Jarib, Zerah, and Shaul.

reuben.name: Reuben
reuben.role: Firstborn whose family appears east of the Jordan
reuben.life: Historical birth and death years are not securely known.
reuben.importance: He is Israel’s firstborn. He defiles his father’s couch, so his birthright goes to Joseph’s sons. His sons are Hanoch, Pallu, Hezron, and Carmi. His families live east of Gilead until Assyria carries them away.
reuben.connections: Son of Jacob and Leah. Brother of Joseph.

joseph.name: Joseph
joseph.role: Ancestor whose sons receive the birthright
joseph.life: Historical birth and death years are not securely known.
joseph.importance: He is a son of Israel. Reuben loses the birthright, and it goes to Joseph’s sons. The prince still comes from Judah.
joseph.connections: Son of Jacob and Rachel. Husband of Asenath. Father of Ephraim and Manasseh.

beerah.name: Beerah
beerah.role: Reubenite leader carried away by Assyria
beerah.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
beerah.importance: He is prince of the Reubenites. Tilgath Pilneser king of Assyria carries him away captive.
beerah.connections: Son of Baal in the line of Joel.

pul.name: Pul
pul.role: Assyrian king who takes the eastern tribes captive
pul.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
pul.importance: Verse 6 says Tilgath Pilneser carries away Beerah, prince of the Reubenites. In verse 26 God stirs up Pul and Tilgath Pilneser. He carries away the Reubenites, the Gadites, and the half-tribe of Manasseh. He brings them to Halah, Habor, Hara, and the river of Gozan.
pul.connections: Verse 26 names both Pul and Tilgath Pilneser as king of Assyria.

jeroboam-ii.name: Jeroboam, son of Joash
jeroboam-ii.role: Northern king used to date a family record
jeroboam-ii.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
jeroboam-ii.importance: Verse 17 names him as king of Israel beside Jotham king of Judah. The families of Gad were listed in their days. The chapter tells no story about him.
jeroboam-ii.connections: Son of Israel’s Joash. Father of Zechariah. Usually called Jeroboam II.

levi.name: Levi
levi.role: Ancestor of priestly and service families
levi.life: Historical birth and death years are not securely known.
levi.importance: His sons are Gershon, Kohath, and Merari. Chapter 6 traces priests, singers, and towns from these three. In chapter 23 David divides the Levites by the same three families.
levi.connections: Son of Israel. Father of Gershon, Kohath, and Merari.

aaron.name: Aaron
aaron.role: Priest whose sons serve at the altar
aaron.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
aaron.importance: He is a son of Amram, and he has four sons. He and his sons offer on the altar and make atonement for Israel. He is set apart to burn incense and to bless in the LORD’s name. David divides his sons’ families for service by lot.
aaron.connections: Son of Amram and Jochebed. Father of Nadab, Abihu, Eleazar, and Ithamar.

moses.name: Moses
moses.role: Servant of God whose commands guide worship
moses.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
moses.importance: He is a son of Amram and the brother of Aaron. The Levites carry the ark on poles, as Moses commanded. The tabernacle he made in the wilderness stands at Gibeon. David tells Solomon to keep the statutes the LORD gave Moses. His sons Gershom and Eliezer are counted with the tribe of Levi.
moses.connections: Son of Amram and Jochebed. Brother of Aaron and Miriam. Husband of Zipporah.

miriam.name: Miriam
miriam.role: Daughter of Amram and sister of Moses and Aaron
miriam.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
miriam.importance: The list names her with Aaron and Moses as a child of Amram. It tells no story about her.
miriam.connections: Daughter of Amram. Sister of Aaron and Moses.

nadab.name: Nadab
nadab.role: Son of Aaron named in the priestly family
nadab.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
nadab.importance: He is the first of Aaron’s four sons in the list. He and Abihu die before their father and have no children. So Eleazar and Ithamar serve as priests.
nadab.connections: Son of Aaron. Brother of Abihu, Eleazar, and Ithamar.

abihu.name: Abihu
abihu.role: Son of Aaron named in the priestly family
abihu.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
abihu.importance: He is the second of Aaron’s four sons in the list. He and Nadab die before their father and have no children. So Eleazar and Ithamar serve as priests.
abihu.connections: Son of Aaron. Brother of Nadab, Eleazar, and Ithamar.

eleazar.name: Eleazar
eleazar.role: Aaron’s son whose family supplies sixteen priest groups
eleazar.life: Historical birth and death years are not securely known.
eleazar.importance: He is Aaron’s third son and the father of Phinehas. Chapter 6 traces the priests from him down to Jehozadak. He serves as priest with Ithamar after Nadab and Abihu die. His family supplies sixteen of the twenty-four groups of priests.
eleazar.connections: Brother of Nadab, Abihu, and Ithamar.

ithamar.name: Ithamar
ithamar.role: Aaron’s son whose family supplies eight priest groups
ithamar.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
ithamar.importance: He is Aaron’s fourth son. He serves as priest with Eleazar after Nadab and Abihu die. His family has eight heads of houses, and Eleazar’s has sixteen. Ahimelech is one of his sons’ line.
ithamar.connections: Brother of Nadab, Abihu, and Eleazar.

phinehas.name: Phinehas
phinehas.role: Priest who once ruled the gatekeepers
phinehas.life: Historical birth and death years are not securely known.
phinehas.importance: He is the son of Eleazar and the father of Abishua. In time past he ruled over the keepers of the entry. Chapter 9 says the LORD was with him.
phinehas.connections: Son of Eleazar. Grandson of Aaron.

samuel.name: Samuel
samuel.role: Seer named in family lists and records
samuel.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
samuel.importance: Chapter 6 names his sons Joel and Abijah. Heman the singer is his grandson. He and David set the gatekeepers in their office of trust. He dedicated gifts that Shelomoth keeps. A history of Samuel the seer records David’s acts.
samuel.connections: Son of Hannah and Elkanah. Father of Joel and Abijah.

heman-singer.name: Heman, the singer
heman-singer.role: Lead singer and the king’s seer
heman-singer.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
heman-singer.importance: He is a Kohathite singer and the grandson of Samuel. The Levites choose him to sound bronze cymbals when the ark moves. He then serves at Gibeon with Jeduthun, with trumpets and cymbals. He is the king’s seer, and his fourteen sons serve in song.
heman-singer.connections: Son of Joel, descendant of Samuel in chapter 6.

asaph-singer.name: Asaph, the singer
asaph-singer.role: Chief of those who give thanks before the ark
asaph-singer.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
asaph-singer.importance: He stands at Heman’s right hand. He sounds cymbals when the ark moves. David makes him chief of the Levites who give thanks before the ark. David leaves him there for each day’s work. His sons later serve under him with harps and cymbals.
asaph-singer.connections: Son of Berechiah. Father of Zaccur, Joseph, Nethaniah, and Asharelah.

ethan-singer.name: Ethan, the singer
ethan-singer.role: Merarite musician beside Heman and Asaph
ethan-singer.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
ethan-singer.importance: He is of the sons of Merari and stands at Heman’s left hand. The Levites choose him with Heman and Asaph. He sounds bronze cymbals when the ark moves.
ethan-singer.connections: Named with Kishi in chapter 6 and Kushaiah in chapter 15.

jehozadak.name: Jehozadak
jehozadak.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
jehozadak.importance: He is the son of Seraiah, last in the list of priests. He goes into captivity when the LORD carries away Judah and Jerusalem. Nebuchadnezzar is the one who takes them.
jehozadak.connections: Son of Seraiah in the priestly list.

ephraim.name: Ephraim
ephraim.role: Ancestor who mourns his killed sons
ephraim.life: Historical birth and death years are not securely known.
ephraim.importance: Men of Gath kill his sons Ezer and Elead in a fight over livestock. He mourns many days, and his brothers come to comfort him. His wife then bears a son, and he names him Beriah. The list then names Sheerah, who builds three towns.
ephraim.connections: Son of Joseph and Asenath. Brother of Manasseh.

manasseh.name: Manasseh
manasseh.role: Ancestor of northern and eastern family branches
manasseh.life: Historical birth and death years are not securely known.
manasseh.importance: His concubine the Aramitess bears Asriel and Machir. Machir is the father of Gilead. The list also names Zelophehad, who has daughters.
manasseh.connections: Son of Joseph and Asenath. Brother of Ephraim.

zelophehad.name: Zelophehad
zelophehad.role: Man whose daughters are noted in Manasseh’s list
zelophehad.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
zelophehad.importance: The list names him in Machir’s family. It says only that he had daughters.
zelophehad.connections: Named in Machir’s family. He has daughters.

sheerah.name: Sheerah
sheerah.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
locations: Beth Horon · upper and lower town region
sheerah.importance: She builds Beth Horon the lower and the upper. She also builds Uzzen Sheerah.
sheerah.connections: Named as Ephraim’s daughter in this family sequence.

joshua.name: Joshua
joshua.role: Son of Nun in Ephraim’s family list
joshua.life: Historical birth and death years are not securely known.
joshua.importance: He is the son of Nun. His name ends a line that runs from Rephah through Elishama and Nun. The list tells no story about him.
joshua.connections: Son of Nun. He later leads Israel in the book of Joshua.

serah.name: Serah
serah.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
serah.importance: She is the sister of Asher’s four sons. The list tells no story about her.
serah.connections: Sister of Imnah, Ishvah, Ishvi, and Beriah.

benjamin.name: Benjamin
benjamin.role: Ancestor of the family line leading to Saul
benjamin.life: Historical birth and death years are not securely known.
benjamin.importance: He is the father of Bela, Ashbel, Aharah, Nohah, and Rapha. The chapter names his families in Geba, Aijalon, Gibeon, and Jerusalem. It ends with Saul’s family.
benjamin.connections: Son of Rachel. Full brother of Joseph.

saul.name: Saul
saul.role: First king whose death leads into David’s reign
saul.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
saul.importance: The Philistines defeat Israel on Mount Gilboa and kill his sons. Archers overtake Saul, and he falls on his sword. The chapter says he died because he did not keep the LORD’s word. The LORD turns the kingdom over to David.
saul.connections: Son of Kish. Father of Jonathan, Merab, Michal, and other children.

jonathan-saul.name: Jonathan
jonathan-saul.role: Saul’s son who dies on Mount Gilboa
jonathan-saul.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
jonathan-saul.importance: The family list names him first among Saul’s sons. His son is Merib-baal. The Philistines kill him with his brothers Abinadab and Malchishua on Mount Gilboa. David’s nephew Jonathan in chapter 20 is another man.
jonathan-saul.connections: Brother of Merab and Michal. Son of Saul.

mephibosheth-jonathan.name: Mephibosheth, Jonathan’s son
mephibosheth-jonathan.role: Merib-baal, Jonathan’s son in Saul’s family
mephibosheth-jonathan.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
mephibosheth-jonathan.importance: The list calls him Merib-baal. He is Jonathan’s son and the father of Micah. Samuel calls him Mephibosheth. The list tells no story about him.
mephibosheth-jonathan.connections: Son of Jonathan and grandson of Saul. Father of Micah.

ishbosheth.name: Ishbosheth
ishbosheth.role: Eshbaal, Saul’s son in the family list
ishbosheth.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
ishbosheth.importance: The list calls him Eshbaal. He is the last of Saul’s four sons in the list. Samuel tells about his rule after Saul’s death.
ishbosheth.connections: Son of Saul. Brother of Jonathan, Malchishua, and Abinadab.

shallum-gatekeeper.name: Shallum, the gatekeeper
shallum-gatekeeper.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
shallum-gatekeeper.importance: He is chief of the gatekeepers. He and his Korahite brothers keep the thresholds of the tent. Their fathers kept the entry of the LORD’s camp. Verse 31 names Mattithiah as the firstborn of Shallum the Korahite.
shallum-gatekeeper.connections: Son of Kore, descendant of Ebiasaph and Korah.

mattithiah-baker.name: Mattithiah, the baker
mattithiah-baker.role: Levite over things baked in pans
mattithiah-baker.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
mattithiah-baker.importance: He is a Levite and the firstborn of Shallum the Korahite. He has the office of trust over the things baked in pans.

saul-armor-bearer.name: Saul’s armor bearer
saul-armor-bearer.role: Unnamed attendant who dies after Saul
saul-armor-bearer.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
saul-armor-bearer.importance: Saul asks him to draw his sword and kill him. He will not, for he is terrified. Saul falls on his own sword. When he sees that Saul is dead, he falls on his sword and dies.
saul-armor-bearer.connections: Companion of Saul in his final battle.

jashobeam.name: Jashobeam
jashobeam.role: Warrior and leader in David’s lists
jashobeam.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
jashobeam.importance: He is chief of the thirty. He lifts his spear against three hundred and kills them at one time. He leads the army division for the first month. A Korahite named Jashobeam joins David at Ziklag, perhaps another man.
jashobeam.connections: Called son of a Hachmonite in chapter 11 and son of Zabdiel in chapter 27.

eleazar-dodai.name: Eleazar
eleazar-dodai.role: Son of Dodo who fights beside David
eleazar-dodai.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
eleazar-dodai.importance: He is with David at Pasdammim when the people flee from the Philistines. They stand in a plot of barley and defend it. They kill the Philistines, and the LORD saves them by a great victory.
eleazar-dodai.connections: Son of Dodo the Ahohite. One of the three mighty men.

benaiah.name: Benaiah
benaiah.role: Son of Jehoiada leading David’s guard and a division
benaiah.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
benaiah.importance: He kills the two sons of Ariel of Moab. He kills a lion in a pit on a snowy day. He takes a tall Egyptian’s spear and kills him with it. David sets him over his guard, and he leads the third month’s division.

uriah.name: Uriah
uriah.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
uriah.importance: The list of mighty men names Uriah the Hittite. It tells no story about him. Samuel tells how David ordered his death.
uriah.connections: Called a Hittite. Husband of Bathsheba.

amasai-warrior.name: Amasai, the warrior
amasai-warrior.role: Chief of the thirty who pledges peace
amasai-warrior.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
amasai-warrior.importance: Men of Benjamin and Judah come to David’s stronghold. David asks if they come to help or to betray him. The Spirit comes on Amasai, and he says, “We are yours, David.” David receives them and makes them captains.
amasai-warrior.connections: Chief of the thirty. He speaks for men of Benjamin and Judah.

zadok.name: Zadok
zadok.role: Priest who serves under David and Solomon
zadok.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
zadok.importance: A young warrior named Zadok comes to David at Hebron with twenty-two captains. David calls Zadok the priest and Abiathar to bring up the ark. Zadok then offers burnt offerings at Gibeon. He helps David divide the priests by lot. The assembly anoints him priest when Solomon is made king.
zadok.connections: Son of Ahitub. Father of Ahimaaz.

abinadab-ark.name: Abinadab
abinadab-ark.role: Man whose house holds the ark
abinadab-ark.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
abinadab-ark.importance: The ark is in his house at Kiriath Jearim. David and all Israel bring it out on a new cart. The chapter tells nothing more about him.
abinadab-ark.connections: The ark is in his house. Uzza and Ahio drive the cart from there.

uzzah.name: Uzza
uzzah.role: Ark attendant who dies during the first journey
uzzah.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
uzzah.importance: He and Ahio drive the cart that carries the ark. The oxen stumble at Chidon’s threshing floor. Uzza puts out his hand to hold the ark. The LORD strikes him, and he dies there. David is afraid and leaves the ark with Obed-Edom.
uzzah.connections: He drives the cart with Ahio from Abinadab’s house.

ahio.name: Ahio
ahio.role: Man who drives the ark cart with Uzza
ahio.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
ahio.importance: He and Uzza drive the new cart from Abinadab’s house. The chapter says nothing more about him.
ahio.connections: He drives the cart with Uzza from Abinadab’s house.

obed-edom.name: Obed Edom
obed-edom.role: Gittite whose house keeps the ark
obed-edom.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
obed-edom.importance: David carries the ark aside into his house. It stays three months, and the LORD blesses his house. David later brings the ark up from his house with joy. Chapter 15 also names an Obed-Edom among the doorkeepers and harp players.

hiram.name: Hiram
hiram.role: King of Tyre who sends cedar and workers
hiram.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
hiram.importance: He sends messengers to David with cedar trees, masons, and carpenters. They are to build David a house. David then sees that the LORD has made him king.
hiram.connections: King of Tyre. He sends messengers to David.

abiathar.name: Abiathar
abiathar.role: Priest David calls to move the ark
abiathar.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
abiathar.importance: David calls Abiathar and Zadok to make ready and bring up the ark. Chapter 27 names him after Ahithophel, the king’s counselor.
abiathar.connections: Priest named with Zadok. Father of Ahimelech in 24:6.

chenaniah-music.name: Chenaniah, the musical leader
chenaniah-music.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
chenaniah-music.importance: He is over the singing when the ark comes up. He teaches the singers because he is skillful. He wears fine linen with the singers and the Levites. Other translations word his task differently.
chenaniah-music.connections: Chief of the Levites. He teaches the singers.

michal.name: Michal
michal.role: Saul’s daughter watching the ark celebration
michal.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
michal.importance: She looks out a window as the ark comes into David’s city. She sees King David dancing and playing. She despises him in her heart.
michal.connections: Daughter of Saul. Wife of David.

jeduthun.name: Jeduthun
jeduthun.role: Musician who gives thanks with the harp
jeduthun.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
jeduthun.importance: He serves at Gibeon with Heman, giving thanks with trumpets and cymbals. His sons are at the gate. Later his sons serve under him in the LORD’s house. He prophesies with the harp, giving thanks and praise to the LORD.
jeduthun.connections: Father of sons who serve in music and at the gate.

obed-edom-jeduthun.name: Obed Edom, son of Jeduthun
obed-edom-jeduthun.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
obed-edom-jeduthun.importance: David leaves him and Hosah as doorkeepers before the ark. The same verse names an Obed-Edom with sixty-eight relatives. The text does not say if they are one man.

hosah.name: Hosah
hosah.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
hosah.importance: David leaves him as a doorkeeper before the ark. He is of the children of Merari. He makes Shimri chief, though Shimri is not the firstborn. The lot gives him and Shuppim the west gate.
hosah.connections: Father of Shimri, Hilkiah, Tebaliah, and Zechariah.

nathan-prophet.name: Nathan
nathan-prophet.role: Prophet who brings God’s answer to David
nathan-prophet.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
nathan-prophet.importance: David tells him that the ark sits in a tent. Nathan says, “Do all that is in your heart.” That night God tells him that David shall not build the house. Nathan tells David that the LORD will build him a house.
nathan-prophet.connections: Prophet who speaks with David. A history of David’s acts bears his name.

hadadezer.name: Hadadezer
hadadezer.role: King of Zobah whom David defeats
hadadezer.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
hadadezer.importance: David defeats him toward Hamath and takes chariots, horsemen, and footmen. David takes his gold shields and much bronze from his cities. Later his captain Shophach leads Syrians against David and dies. His servants then make peace with David and serve him.
hadadezer.connections: King of Zobah. Syrians of Damascus come to help him. Shophach is his captain.

toi.name: Tou
toi.role: Tou, king of Hamath who greets David
toi.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
toi.importance: He hears that David has struck Hadadezer’s army. Hadadezer had wars with Tou. He sends his son Hadoram to greet and bless David. Hadoram brings vessels of gold, silver, and bronze.
toi.connections: Father of Hadoram. Hadadezer had wars with him.

joram-hamath.name: Hadoram
joram-hamath.role: Hadoram, Tou’s son sent to David
joram-hamath.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
joram-hamath.importance: His father Tou sends him to greet and bless King David. He brings vessels of gold, silver, and bronze. David dedicates them to the LORD.
joram-hamath.connections: Son of Tou king of Hamath.

ahimelech-abiathar.name: Ahimelech, son of Abiathar
ahimelech-abiathar.role: Priest who helps divide the priests
ahimelech-abiathar.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
ahimelech-abiathar.importance: Verse 18:16 calls him Abimelech and lists him as priest with Zadok. He is of the sons of Ithamar. He helps David and Zadok divide the priests for service. He is present when Shemaiah writes the lots.
ahimelech-abiathar.connections: Son of Abiathar in 24:6. Called Abimelech in the reading of 18:16.

shavsha.name: Shavsha
shavsha.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
shavsha.importance: The list of David’s officials names him as scribe. It tells no story about him.
shavsha.connections: Named with Joab, Zadok, and Benaiah.

hanun.name: Hanun
hanun.role: Ammonite king who shames David’s messengers
hanun.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
hanun.importance: His father Nahash dies, and David sends men to comfort him. His princes say the men came to spy. Hanun shaves them, cuts their garments, and sends them away. He then hires chariots and horsemen, and war follows.

nahash.name: Nahash
nahash.role: Ammonite king who was kind to David
nahash.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
nahash.importance: He dies, and his son reigns in his place. David says that Nahash showed him kindness. So David sends men to comfort Hanun.
nahash.connections: King of the children of Ammon. Father of Hanun.

shophach.name: Shophach
shophach.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
shophach.importance: He leads the Syrians who come from beyond the River. David crosses the Jordan and fights them. The Syrians flee, and David kills Shophach.
shophach.connections: Captain of the army of Hadadezer.

sibbecai.name: Sibbecai
sibbecai.role: Warrior who kills Sippai and leads a division
sibbecai.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
sibbecai.importance: The list of mighty men names Sibbecai the Hushathite. In the war at Gezer he kills Sippai, of the sons of the giant. The Philistines are subdued. He leads the army division for the eighth month. Samuel gives a different name for the man he kills.

elhanan-jair.name: Elhanan, son of Jair
elhanan-jair.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
elhanan-jair.importance: He kills Lahmi, the brother of Goliath the Gittite. Samuel’s parallel verse uses different names. Chapter 11 names an Elhanan who is the son of Dodo.
elhanan-jair.connections: Son of Jair in this chapter.

lahmi.name: Lahmi
lahmi.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
lahmi.importance: He is the brother of Goliath the Gittite. Elhanan kills him in a war with the Philistines. Samuel’s parallel verse has different wording.

jonathan-shimei.name: Jonathan, David’s nephew
jonathan-shimei.role: David’s nephew who kills a giant at Gath
jonathan-shimei.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
jonathan-shimei.importance: A man of great stature at Gath has twenty-four fingers and toes. He defies Israel. Jonathan kills him.
jonathan-shimei.connections: Son of Shimea, David’s brother, in 20:7.

goliath.name: Goliath
goliath.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
goliath.importance: The chapter names him only as Lahmi’s brother. It calls him Goliath the Gittite. In this verse Elhanan kills Lahmi.
goliath.connections: Called the Gittite. Brother of Lahmi.

gad.name: Gad
gad.role: David’s seer who brings a choice and a command
gad.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
gad.importance: The LORD tells him to offer David three things. Gad names them: famine, enemies, or pestilence. Later the angel tells Gad to send David to Ornan’s threshing floor. David goes and builds an altar there. A history of Gad the seer records David’s acts.
gad.connections: David’s seer. He carries the LORD’s words to David.

araunah.name: Ornan
araunah.role: Ornan, Jebusite owner of the threshing floor
araunah.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
araunah.importance: He is threshing wheat when he sees the angel. David asks to buy the threshing floor. Ornan offers it free, with oxen, wood, and wheat. David pays six hundred shekels of gold and builds an altar.
araunah.connections: A Jebusite. Father of four sons. He deals with David.

ornan-sons.name: Ornan’s four sons
ornan-sons.role: Four unnamed sons who hide from the angel
ornan-sons.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
ornan-sons.importance: They are with Ornan while he threshes wheat. Ornan sees the angel, and they hide.
ornan-sons.connections: Four sons with Ornan at the threshing floor.

gershom-moses.name: Gershom, Moses’ son
gershom-moses.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
gershom-moses.importance: He is a son of Moses. His son Shebuel is chief and rules over the treasuries. The list tells no story about him.
gershom-moses.connections: Son of Moses. Father of Shebuel.

eliezer-moses.name: Eliezer, Moses’ son
eliezer-moses.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
eliezer-moses.importance: He is a son of Moses. He has one son, Rehabiah, whose sons are very many. Shelomoth, who keeps the dedicated things, comes from him.
eliezer-moses.connections: Son of Moses. Father of Rehabiah.

shemaiah-scribe.name: Shemaiah, the scribe
shemaiah-scribe.role: Levite who writes down the priests’ lots
shemaiah-scribe.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
shemaiah-scribe.importance: He is a Levite, the son of Nethanel. He writes down the lots for the priests. He does so before the king, the princes, Zadok, and Ahimelech.

obed-edom-gatekeeper.name: Obed Edom, the gatekeeper
obed-edom-gatekeeper.role: Head of a family that keeps a gate and storehouse
obed-edom-gatekeeper.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
obed-edom-gatekeeper.importance: He has eight sons, “for God blessed him.” Sixty-two of his family are able men for the service. The lot gives him the south gate and his sons the storehouse. The text does not say if he is the Gittite of chapter 13.
obed-edom-gatekeeper.connections: Father of eight sons named in chapter 26.

meshelemiah.name: Meshelemiah
meshelemiah.role: Head of a family of gatekeepers
meshelemiah.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
meshelemiah.importance: He is a Korahite, the son of Kore. He has seven sons, and Zechariah is the firstborn. The east gate falls by lot to Shelemiah, another form of his name. Zechariah, a wise counselor, receives the north gate.
meshelemiah.connections: Son of Kore. Father of Zechariah and six other named sons.

shelomoth-treasurer.name: Shelomoth, the treasurer
shelomoth-treasurer.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
shelomoth-treasurer.importance: He and his brothers are over the treasuries of the dedicated things. David and the captains dedicated plunder to repair the LORD’s house. Samuel, Saul, Abner, and Joab also dedicated gifts. All of it is under his hand.
shelomoth-treasurer.connections: From the family of Eliezer, the son of Moses.

shebuel-treasurer.name: Shebuel, the treasurer
shebuel-treasurer.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
shebuel-treasurer.importance: He is the son of Gershom, the son of Moses. He is chief among Gershom’s sons. He is ruler over the treasuries.
shebuel-treasurer.connections: Son of Gershom, the son of Moses.

abner.name: Abner
abner.role: Son of Ner who dedicated gifts
abner.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
abner.importance: He dedicated gifts, and Shelomoth keeps them. The chapter tells nothing more about him.
abner.connections: Son of Ner. Named beside Saul among those who dedicated gifts.

ahithophel.name: Ahithophel
ahithophel.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
ahithophel.importance: The list calls him the king’s counselor. After him come Jehoiada the son of Benaiah, and Abiathar. The list tells no story about him.
ahithophel.connections: The king’s counselor. Jehoiada and Abiathar come after him.

hushai.name: Hushai
hushai.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
hushai.importance: The list calls Hushai the Archite the king’s friend. It tells no story about him.
hushai.connections: Called the Archite. Named beside Ahithophel.

obil.name: Obil
obil.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
obil.importance: He is over King David’s camels. The list tells no story about him.

jaziz.name: Jaziz
jaziz.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
jaziz.importance: He is over King David’s flocks. The list tells no story about him.

jehiel-treasurer.name: Jehiel, the Gershonite
jehiel-treasurer.role: Gershonite who keeps the precious stones
jehiel-treasurer.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
jehiel-treasurer.importance: People who have precious stones give them for the LORD’s house. The stones go into the treasure under Jehiel’s hand.
